tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms/intent (failed eval job, swinging judge scores, incomparable scores, no AWS-doc evidence of evaluation), and explicitly lists trigger contexts including implicit ones ('even if they do not mention eval recipes, judge models, temperature...'). It also clarifies scope boundary (Bedrock CreateEvaluationJob routes elsewhere). While dense, it stays within a reasonable paragraph length typical for a complex routing skill.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when such an evaluation job fails or cannot start on an instance limit, judge scores swing between runs on the same model, benchmark scores look far better than real use, scores of successive model versions cannot be compared, a domain-specific metric no built-in covers is needed, or a fine-tuned model is about to ship and nobody can say it was evaluated...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays in domain-specific territory throughout — check-ids, routing rules, API quirks, guardrails — without explaining general concepts like what SageMaker or evaluation jobs are. It is dense but not padded with things the agent already knows.
tests.evidence: Every finding carries a stable `check-id`, a severity, and an AWS-doc citation. You never invent a threshold: a judgment with no AWS-published number is marked `workload-specific`

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The check table, router table, and known-causes content are indexes/pointers with short descriptions, not the detailed rules themselves — the body explicitly defers the full detection rules, remediations, and citations to references/ files.
tests.evidence: The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five files in references/ are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a clear trigger condition for when to load it, e.g. tied to router symptoms or specific review steps.
tests.evidence: Load [known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md) whenever the user names an error or symptom; match it to a section, check the cited AWS page, and give the cause, how to confirm it, and the fix.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (guardrails, read-only enforcement, severity invention) are stated as strict non-negotiables, while diagnostic reasoning (break-fix, router) explains purpose and lets the agent match symptoms flexibly.
tests.evidence:
Non-negotiable, at every step:
1. **Read-only.** A SageMaker-side eval runs as a training job, so never call `CreateTrainingJob`, `StopTrainingJob`, or any other mutating API.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tools/approaches as equal menus; the router and check tables each point to a single matched path per symptom.
tests.evidence: Router table maps each 'Operator says' row to one specific 'First read' and 'Load' action, not multiple equal options.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic procedure (match symptom → confirm via collection calls → report with check-id) applicable to any SageMaker eval job, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: There is a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section plus an Error Handling section covering non-obvious traps like CloudWatch's absent-datapoints behavior, functioning as a gotchas section.
tests.evidence: "This is an evaluation request, so it is mine to catalogue." ... "No evaluation metrics were found, so the scores are zero." Absent datapoints in `LLMOps/Evaluation` mean the scores were never published, not a measured zero.

tests.evidence:
Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion.
- [ ] Every finding carries a matching **`check-id`**...
